rationale: Escitalopram (SSRI; t½ ~27h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk) to vortioxetine (SMS; multimodal serotonergic; t½ ~66h). Reasons: cognitive impairment on escitalopram, sexual dysfunction, or partial response with desire for multimodal augmentation. Both are serotonergic — low but non-zero serotonin syndrome risk during brief overlap at standard doses. Escitalopram is not a CYP2D6 inhibitor — no dose adjustment needed for vortioxetine. Direct switch strategy: stop escitalopram and start vortioxetine on the same day. A very brief taper of escitalopram is included to reduce discontinuation syndrome risk. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start vortioxetine 10 mg. Reduce escitalopram to 10 mg (halving before stopping reduces discontinuation syndrome). Both at reduced dose for 7 days. Escitalopram is not a CYP2D6 inhibitor — no vortioxetine dose adjustment needed.
Stop escitalopram. Continue vortioxetine 10 mg. Monitor for escitalopram discontinuation symptoms (usually mild at this point). Titrate vortioxetine to 20 mg at 2–4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Escitalopram 20 mg → vortioxetine 10 mg (standard effective starting doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
